correctness.rationale: For n>=4, every proper named 3-colouring is in exactly one of three types (two monochromatic sides; one bichromatic and one monochromatic side; or a unique matched nonedge bearing a shared colour). This follows from the fact that any colour on both shores can occur only at one matched nonedge, and two such shared colours would force an improper cross-edge among at least two remaining indices. Type I demands all 2n seeds. In Type II all n bichromatic-side vertices must be seeded; the matched opposite vertex is compulsory exactly if one side colour occurs once. In Type III the two shared-colour vertices and one additional seed are necessary and sufficient; the explicit three-stage forcing sequence requires n-2>=2. Distinct terminal colourings cannot share a successful partial assignment, because each forced colour is the sole proper possibility. These facts yield the exact H_n(z) and coefficient 12n(n-1) at z^3. For K_{n,n}, every colour class has one shore and all n vertices of the two-colour shore must be seeded in any successful 3-colour completion, giving sharp minimum n. The self-contained verifier exhaustively checked the H_n formula for n=4,5 (1,114,112 partial assignments) and the n=3 exclusion. Finite checking supplements, not proves, the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality: Farr defines the locally forced-colouring polynomial and supplies properties and small-graph examples, not this two-parameter crown-family exact enumerator. Existing published exact forced three-colour formulas for complete bipartite hosts and complete multipartite hosts assume all relevant cross-edges exist; their statements do not imply the matching-deleted host result, where shared-colour pairs permit new three-seed configurations. Degree-two classifications apply to Cr_3=C_6 and do not cover Cr_n for n>=4. Other crown graph colouring results use different parity or conflict-free conditions. Searches for the precise host, related graph aliases and the same forced-colouring invariant found no equivalent statement. Absence from indexed searches is not a proof of worldwide novelty; a hidden earlier equivalent precolouring result remains a risk.

value.rationale: The exact z-generating polynomial enumerates every successful initial partial named three-colouring on an infinite natural dense bipartite family, rather than merely its minimum. The matching-deleted graph has a new shared-pair terminal state; a structural exact characterization leads to a three-seed formula and an explicit unbounded contrast n versus 3 against K_{n,n}, making the combinatorial sensitivity substantive and motivated by a newly introduced graph polynomial. The case n=3 and other palettes are explicitly excluded; no claimed broad graph classification is needed for this complete, nontrivial infinite-family result.
